text:
For this protocol, a suitable diagnostic is a paired, category-stratified user bootstrap: retain each user’s two models’ binary hit@10 outcomes, resample the same user indices for both models within each category, then average the four category differences equally. Report the observed macro difference, a 95% bootstrap interval, and category differences. Pairing preserves within-user dependence ([SciPy bootstrap documentation](https://cache-docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. This proposed interval conditions on fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates; it excludes training-seed variability, candidate-resampling variability, and generalization to new datasets. Shared users across categories would require coordinated resampling.

Repeated checkpoint and architecture selection on the same validation users can overfit validation noise. A bootstrap interval computed after selecting the winner does not correct that selection bias; small gains remain exploratory, especially after many adaptive comparisons. Record search breadth and reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation ([Cawley and Talbot, 2010](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures success within that candidate protocol. Krichene and Rendle show sampled metrics can reverse model ordering relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation; low sampling variance does not eliminate this bias ([On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged, but describe gains specifically as fixed-candidate validation improvements. They do not establish better full-catalog recommendations for the simulator’s users.
